facts.fact: 叙述者说昨晚她又从窗口看到了田野里的篝火。
facts.anchor: I saw the fires from my window again last night.

facts.fact: 这些篝火年复一年准时燃起，她每年都以为会是最后一次。
facts.anchor: Every year, like clockwork, they blaze on, and every year I expect it to be the last.

facts.fact: 她说镇民知道的不是她的故事，但她的故事会在这座房子里留存，由她来讲。
facts.anchor: It’s not my story they know. But it’s my story that will linger in this house long after I am gone, and it is mine to tell.

facts.fact: 她承认嫁给 Alexander S— 太快了，人人都同意。
facts.anchor: I married Alexander S— much too quickly. Everyone would agree on that.

facts.fact: 第一次四目相对时，她感到像一片冰扎进心脏，整个人悬在半空。
facts.anchor: I felt as though a shard of ice had penetrated my heart, as though my very being was being held in suspense, frozen in a second in time.

facts.fact: Mrs Hayworth 介绍她时总用全名 Maria Isabel，她多次要求只叫她 Isabel 也没用。
facts.anchor: no matter how many times I asked her to call me simply Isabel.

facts.fact: 第二天早上他派人送来邀请，请她下午一起沿海滨散步。
facts.anchor: Would I join him for a walk along the promenade in the afternoon?

facts.fact: 在海滨他称她 Ms Smith，问她觉得苏格兰怎么样。
facts.anchor: ‘How do you find Scotland, Ms Smith?’

facts.fact: 他问她找父亲的进展，她比预想更诚实地回答「不知道」。
facts.anchor: ‘I don’t know,’ I answered, more truthfully than I had intended.

facts.fact: 结尾她说自己当时被情绪淹没，没想过他的情绪可能与她的截然不同。
facts.anchor: I did not, in my overwhelmed state, consider the possibility that his could be that much different than mine.
